newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Moolen buys German, Swiss market makers.
newsitem.headline: Moolen buys German, Swiss market makers.

text.p: Securities trader Van der Moolen said on Friday it had bought a 75 percent stake in Germany's Agon GmbH and Switzerland's Quotic AG for an undisclosed sum.
Both firms operate under one management as market makers on the German DTB and Swiss Soffex electronic derivatives exchanges. Agon and Quotic have a total of 20 traders.
Van der Moolen said the deal fitted its strategy to strengthen option and share trading in electronic markets.
"Agon and Quotic will aim at further growth within continental Europe and are expected to contribute to Van der Moolen's earnings per share this year," the company said.

Van der Moolen said U.S. equities house LaBranche & Co, in which it owned a 24.9 percent stake, had agreed to merge with two other market specialist on the New York Stock Exchange, Stern Bros and Ernst & Co.
"This transaction wil substantially increase LaBranche's income," Van der Moolen said. It added it would own an interest of about 19 percent in the merged firm.
Income growth would compensate for the smaller stake in the newly combined firm, it said.
